entities.summary:
John Tiptoft, 1st Earl of Worcester KG, was an English nobleman and scholar who served as Lord High Treasurer, Lord High Constable of England and Lord Deputy of Ireland. He was known as "the Butcher of England" to his Tudor detractors.

Tiptoft was born in unknown and died on October 18, 1470, at the age of 44. He was a member of the powerful Tiptoft family, which had strong ties to the royal court. His early life and education are not well documented, but it is known that he studied at Oxford University and later served as a diplomat in Europe.

As Lord High Treasurer, Tiptoft was responsible for managing the royal finances and overseeing the administration of the kingdom. He was also a key figure in the Wars of the Roses, playing a crucial role in the Battle of Barnet in 1471. His involvement in the conflict led to his eventual downfall, as he was accused of treachery and was killed during the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485.

Tiptoft's legacy is complex and multifaceted. On the one hand, he was a skilled politician and administrator who played a significant role in shaping the course of English history. On the other hand, his involvement in the Wars of the Roses and his later treachery have left a lasting stain on his reputation.

Today, Tiptoft is remembered as a significant figure in English history, particularly in the context of the Wars of the Roses. His life and career serve as a reminder of the complexities and nuances of medieval politics.
